_comment: Fine-texture powder coat: a polyester powder sprayed onto metal and baked into one continuous pigmented film, the finish of architectural panels, ribs, railings and window frames. Authored white, so a Creator tints it to any colour (author light). Opaque, with no coat: unlike gloss paint the film has no clear top, it is one matte-to-satin layer whose surface cures into a dense field of small rounded bumps a few tenths of a millimetre across. That is what keeps it from reading as plastic: a soft, even satin with no sharp highlight. The maps are generated (L2, gen_powdercoat_textured.py). BUILT TO STAY EVEN ON LARGE PANELS: the 1 cm tile carries nothing slower than the bumps, so there is no mottle to repeat, and the satin is in the roughness itself, so it holds when the bumps fall below a pixel. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): scratches (overlay 1, damage), dust as a deposit (Phase10), fingerprints, placed by the Edges mask, whose channels fit the row's order (G damage along borders, B deposit in corners, A handling on open faces). Not carried: the chalking an old powder coat shows outdoors. Built for the platform's generated architectural Set (261004_R_PlatformSetMaterialAsks.md, A4).

sources.why: Physically Based has no powder coat entry. The colour is a neutral white of linear albedo 0.82 (the generated basecolor's mean): an architectural white of light reflectance about 84 to 87, less the few percent the surface reflects. Roughness about 0.55 in the map for a fine-texture grade, which is matte to satin; no measured value. specular_ior 1.5 for a polyester resin film, the value Physically Based's Car Paint gives for an acrylic enamel.
